# ff-tracking

**A virtual camera films an AI agent's screen while a tracker locks onto every glyph it types.**

Six seconds, two [fframes](https://github.com/dmtrKovalenko/fframes) passes, one SkSL shader.
No footage, no stock audio: every pixel and every sound comes from code.

 
 
 
 

 
 
 

**[▶ Full 1080p with sound](https://github.com/mrsarac/ff-tracking/releases/download/v1.0.0/tracking.mp4)** ·
[On X](https://x.com/0xsarac/status/2108515856544317489) ·
[How it works](#how-it-works) ·
[Quick start](#quick-start)

**Part 2 → [ff-unmute](https://github.com/mrsarac/ff-unmute): the one you can unmute. Music written in code, every number on screen measured from the sound.**

 fframes studies · #1 ff-tracking · #2 ff-unmute , the one you can unmute 

## What you are looking at

An agent thinks out loud in a terminal: `thinking…` → `reading 14 files` →
`tool_call: render_frame()` → … → `✓ 0 problems` → `Done`. A computer-vision style tracker
follows the newest characters. A camera that never sits still films the screen up close.

- **Real coordinates.** Every `x: 1403 y: 559` label is the box's actual pixel position in
 that frame of the output. None of them are random numbers.
- **Focus that follows the tracker.** The focal plane is set by the box being tracked, so
 the depth of field racks along the line as the agent types.
- **Chain of thought, drawn.** Links run from box to box in reading order, and a dot runs
 along every link.
- **The lock.** Every shot ends with the newest word locking on: red for two frames, a
 scanline tear, a beep panned to where the box is.
- **Twelve shots, twelve looks.** A cut every 0.5 s through paper white, thermal, black
 and white, phosphor, amber, navy and neon.
- **A collapse and a landing.** Fourteen boxes fall into one, and that box becomes a
 `Done` pill before the fade to black.

 

## How it works

```text
hud ──► flat pass 1: SVG, 3840×2160 ─────────► out/pass/flat.mp4 ──┐ iChannel0
 │ ▼
 ├────► lens pass 2: SkSL on Skia Metal + camera tracker ──► out/tracking.mp4
 │ ▲ audio
 └────► tracks ──► out/tracks.json ──► sfx.py ──► out/pass/sfx.wav ─────┘
```

**Pass 1, `flat`**, draws the screen the way a terminal would: black, white, monospace, one
` ` per glyph, so the position of every character is known exactly. The tracker boxes
are on the screen itself. Some are hatched with an SVG pattern in `mix-blend-mode:
difference`, so the stripes turn dark where they cross a glyph. The only color is pure red,
and it marks a locked box. The pass renders at 2× because the lens magnifies it up to 3×.

**Pass 2, `lens`**, binds each frame of pass 1 as a shader input and films it. One SkSL
shader does everything physical:

 

1. **Perspective.** Every pixel shoots a ray at a tilted plane: real perspective, not an SVG skew.
2. **Depth of field.** The circle of confusion comes from the depth difference to the tracked
 target, with 36 golden-angle taps and highlights weighted like bokeh.
3. **Palette and aberration.** Brightness maps through five color stops per shot. R, G and B
 sample at radially shifted points, and the shift grows on a lock.
4. **Bloom and LED grid.** A wide ring of taps lifts everything around bright glyphs. The
 grid uses equal-area RGB stripes, so it adds no tint, and it fades out of focus.
5. **Tear, grain, camera tracker.** Rows slide on a lock and right after a cut. On top, the
 lens draws its own tracker sharp: links, labels and target brackets, projected with
 `hud::project`, the CPU copy of the shader's camera.

Both passes and the sound read the same `hud` crate, so the lens always knows where the
glyph it focuses on actually is.

**Sound**: `tools/sfx.py` reads `out/tracks.json` and synthesizes everything. It makes a
screen hum, a bit-crushed glitch on each cut, a click per keystroke and a pentatonic beep
per lock, panned to the box. It adds a riser into the collapse and a chime with a sub hit on
`Done`. Loudness is measured with ffmpeg's `ebur128` and set to -14 LUFS.

**Score** (optional): [`score/score.py`](score/score.py) is a second soundtrack, made in
[Slab](https://github.com/nooga/slab): a darker, heavier piece at 120 BPM, so every cut lands
on a beat. It reads the same `out/tracks.json`, plus `out/camera.json` from the `camera`
binary, so the mix follows the lens. The tracked box pans the lock blips and keystrokes, the
screen's slide pans the pad, riser and glitches, each zoom push opens the bass filter, and the
red lock frames tear the bass. See [Slab score](#slab-score).

## Quick start

macOS uses Metal; Windows uses Vulkan. For Windows requirements and the PowerShell
render pipeline, see [Windows setup](docs/WINDOWS.md). The macOS instructions follow.

Requirements: macOS with Apple silicon (Skia on Metal), Rust, ffmpeg, Python 3 with `numpy`
and `scipy`. The README images also need Pillow and `img2webp`.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/mrsarac/ff-tracking && cd ff-tracking
tools/render.sh # → out/tracking.mp4
```

`render.sh` builds the workspace, exports the tracks, renders pass 1, synthesizes the sound
and renders pass 2. It takes about 40 s on an M3 Pro, plus the first build.

Every pass is an fframes CLI, so the usual tools work on each of them:

```bash
target/release/lens strip all -n 12 # contact sheet of the final video
target/release/lens frame 81 -o frames # one full-size frame
target/release/lens preview # real-time window with sound
target/release/lens audio analyze # loudness, true peak
LENS_STAGE=1 target/release/lens frame 81 # stop the shader after a step (0-3), as in the image above
python3 -I tools/readme_media.py # rebuild the images in this README
```

## Slab score

`tools/score.sh` is `render.sh` with the Slab score in place of `sfx.py`:

```bash
tools/score.sh # uses the committed render, score/score.wav
SLAB=/path/to/slab tools/score.sh # renders the score again from score/score.py
```

Rendering needs a [Slab](https://github.com/nooga/slab) checkout built with
`zig build -Doptimize=Releas

# lintapple

It should be impossible for AI to make a bad UI.

[npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/lintapple) · [Demo](https://lintapple.vercel.app/)

## Install

Requires Node.js 22 or later. Run in your app’s project directory:

```sh
npm install -D lintapple && npx lintapple init
```

This creates `ui-policy.json` and a `lint:ui` script. Existing settings are kept.
Set the fonts and text sizes in `ui-policy.json` to match your app. Set the app URL in the `lint:ui` script; the default is `http://localhost:3000`.

## Use

Start your app, then run:

```sh
npm run lint:ui
```

Each finding includes the rule, element, measured value, and suggested fix.
Exit codes: `0` passed, `1` findings, `2` check did not finish.

To check another URL or save a JSON report:

```sh
npx lintapple http://localhost:3000 --json
```

For a page that loads asynchronously, add `--ready '[data-app-ready]'` with a selector that is visible when the page is ready.

## Use in Playwright

Add this to an existing test after the page is ready:

```js
import { expectUI } from 'lintapple/playwright';

await expectUI(page, testInfo);
```

Findings fail the test and attach a JSON report. The helper reads your `ui-policy.json`.
See the [example tests](examples/playwright/).

## Mark layout elements

Font, contrast, control size, and screen bounds checks work without extra markup.
Add these attributes for checks that need layout information:

| Attribute | Use on |
| --- | --- |
| `data-ui-stack` | A group whose child spacing must be checked. |
| `data-ui-actions` | A button group whose gaps must be checked. |
| `data-ui-container` | A surface whose button insets must be checked. |
| `data-ui-number` | A changing number that needs equal digit widths. |
| `data-ui-content` | A container whose text must stay inside its edges. |
| `data-ui-align="start"` | A group whose marked elements must align. Use `center` or `end` for other alignments. |
| `data-ui-align-item` | Each element to compare in an alignment group. |
| `data-ui-radius` | An outer surface with equal corner radii and insets. |
| `data-ui-radius-inner` | Its direct inner surface. Its radius must equal the outer radius minus the inset. |

You can also use `controlContainers` in the policy to select existing button containers.
See [example styles](examples/ui.css).

## License

MIT. See [LICENSE](https://github.com/gholtzap/lintapple/blob/main/LICENSE).

half144/overdrive-releases.text:
Overdrive is a game store that runs on a jailbroken PS5. Browse the catalog, download with up to 64
connections at once, extract archives and hand finished games to ShadowMountPlus, all from the
controller.

This repository holds its builds. Install it once by hand; after that, Overdrive updates itself.

## Support Overdrive

Help us host the games ourselves on our own CDN (Cloudflare) for much faster downloads.

 https://ko-fi.com/overdrivebaby

> **Upgrading from the folder install?** It will stop getting updates soon. Follow
> [MIGRATE.md](MIGRATE.md) to switch to the single-file image.

## What you need

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **A jailbroken PS5** | Tested on firmware 13.60 |
| **[ShadowMountPlus](https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus)** | Registers Overdrive and the games it downloads |
| **An ELF loader on port 9021** | For example John Törnblom's elfldr. Overdrive uses it to install packages, and a folder install to reopen itself after an update |
| **A way to copy files to the console** | FTP, [PS5Upload](https://github.com/phantomptr/ps5upload) or a USB drive |

## Install

1. **Download** `Overdrive-PPSA99058.exfat.zip` from the [latest release](https://github.com/half144/overdrive-releases/releases/latest).
2. **Unzip** it on your computer. You get a single file, `Overdrive-PPSA99058.exfat`: the whole app
 in one exFAT image.
3. **Copy** that file to `/data/homebrew/` on the console (or to `homebrew/` on a USB drive plugged
 into it), so you end up with `/data/homebrew/Overdrive-PPSA99058.exfat`. Do not change its
 permissions: ShadowMountPlus mounts the image as it is.
 - **FTP:** connect to the console's FTP server and upload the file into `/data/homebrew/`.
 - **PS5Upload:** send the file with `/data/homebrew/` as the destination folder.
 - **USB:** copy the file to `homebrew/` at the root of an exFAT drive and plug it into the console.
4. **Register** it: with ShadowMountPlus running, Overdrive appears on the home screen within a few
 seconds. If it does not, run ShadowMountPlus's scan again.
5. **Open** Overdrive from the home screen.

> Keep the file name `Overdrive-PPSA99058.exfat`, and keep only one copy of Overdrive: if you had
> the folder install, delete `/data/homebrew/PPSA99058` first so ShadowMount doesn't see two copies.
> [MIGRATE.md](MIGRATE.md) walks through switching from the folder install.

 
 Alternative: the folder install (deprecated) 

The folder install will stop getting updates soon; prefer the image above, or
[switch to it](MIGRATE.md) if you already have the folder.

1. Download `Overdrive-PPSA99058.zip` from the latest release and extract it: you get a folder named
 `PPSA99058`.
2. Copy the whole folder to `/data/homebrew/`, so you end up with
 `/data/homebrew/PPSA99058/eboot.bin`. Keep the folder name: it is the title ID.
3. Set the folder's permissions to `777`, recursively. FTP clients such as zftpd write files as
 `0666`, which the console's loader refuses ("Cannot start the game or app").
4. Register and open it as above.
 

## Updates

Overdrive checks this repository a few seconds after it opens. When a newer release is out, it
asks first:

```
UPDATE AVAILABLE
v0.0.89
v0.0.88 → v0.0.89
[ Update now ] [ Later ]
```

**Update now** downloads the release, checks it against the SHA-256 GitHub publishes for it,
and installs it. An image install gets the new image in place of the old one: Overdrive then
closes, and ShadowMountPlus mounts the new image when you open it again from the home screen after
a few seconds. A
folder install gets the new files swapped into its folder and reopens on its own. Your downloads,
favorites and settings stay where they are.

To update by hand instead, repeat the install steps over the existing file (or folder).

## Troubleshooting

 
 "Cannot start the game or app" after copying the folder 

Only the folder install has this: the console's launcher needs to read every file in the folder.
Set the folder's permissions to `777`, recursively (most FTP clients and PS5Upload can do it), then
open Overdrive again. The image install never needs it.
 

 
 Overdrive closes after an update but does not reopen 

With the image install that is expected: open Overdrive from the home screen. With the folder
install, reopening needs the ELF loader on port 9021; without it the update still installs, and
Overdrive runs the new version when you open it.

If you reopen an image install too fast, the old version may open and offer the same update again:
choose **Later**, close Overdrive and open it again after a few seconds. ShadowMountPlus releases
the old image a moment after the app closes.
 

 
 The update dialog never appears 

The console needs internet access to reach GitHub, and Overdrive only offers a release newer than
the version shown next to its logo. GitHub allows 60 checks an hour per network; a busy shared
connection can run out, and the next launch tries again.
 

 
 Overdrive does not show up on the home screen 

Check that ShadowMountPlus is running and that the path is exactly
`/data/homebrew/Overdrive-PPSA99058.exfat` (or, for the folder install,
`/data/homebrew/PPSA99058/eboot.bin`, not one folder deeper). If both the image and the
`PPSA99058` folder are there, ShadowMountPlus sees the same title twice: delete the folder.
 

 
 Every download fails with "No connection to the server" (or "Not enough free space" with plenty of room) 

The console can't resolve the download servers' names, so every download stops at 0 MB. Covers
may still load, because Overdrive looks their addresses up on its own; downloads use the console's
DNS.

- **DNS set to `127.0.0.1`** (common with Y2JB and other jailbreak setups): that address is a DNS
 payload running on the console, such as NanoDNS. Load it before opening Overdrive, then choose
 **Retry**.
- **Any other DNS**: set the console's DNS to `1.1.1.1` and `1.0.0.1` (or `8.8.8.8` and `8.8.4.4`)
 in **Settings > Network > Settings > Set Up Internet Connection**, then choose **

zhouwei713/luobo-ppt.text:
# 萝卜 PPT.skill

> *丢进来一篇文章或一份旧 PPT，拿回去一份能直接改字的原生 PPT。*

 
 
 
 
 

 

**一个做 PPT 和美化 PPT 的 Agent Skill。**

从零生成时，给它一个题目、一篇文章、一份口播稿或大纲，它先写出结论式标题和口播备注，再排版出图。
按参考图美化时，给它一份朴素的 .pptx 和一张参考图，它把原文一字不改地搬进统一的配色、版式、图标和插画里，少一个字都不交。

 

[效果示例](#效果示例) · [安装](#安装) · [使用方式](#使用方式) · [它解决什么](#它解决什么) · [工作原理](#工作原理) · [14 套风格](#14-套风格)

## 效果示例

### 文字一个不动，换身衣服

上面一排是原稿，下面一排是给了一张薄荷绿参考图之后美化出来的。标题、要点、数字一个字都没改，换掉的是配色、版式、图标和插画。

 

### 同一份原稿，换一张参考图就是另一套风格

从上往下依次是原稿、薄荷参考图、深色科技、墨水杂志。四个版本文字完全一样。

 

### 参考图里有什么，封面就画什么

参考图是一张环保科普封面，山坡上立着风车。美化后的封面照着参考图的元素画出了风景，整张图没接任何 AI 生图模型，是程序画出来的。

 

### 理科课件，公式一个不丢

一份高中数学导数复习课，原稿里有 12 个用公式编辑器打的公式，在 LibreOffice 里打开全是空白。解析时它会把这类公式转成普通文字公式，换什么软件都看得到，也能直接改字。

 

 

### 一篇文章，直接变成能讲的 PPT

把一篇公众号文章丢给它，生成 15 页的口播 PPT。它先写一份只有标题的"幽灵稿"让你确认，每页标题都是一句结论，每页都带口播备注。

 

### 数据、流程、分析框架也装得下

时间线、漏斗、中心辐射、2x2 矩阵、原生表格、原生图表，外加 SWOT、PEST、波特五力、商业画布。表格是真表格，图表双击就能改数据。

 

### 工具教程的截图有专门的版式

一张截图配几条说明，说明里写上位置，截图上就打一个对应的编号点。几张截图走一个流程，按各自的宽高比分配宽度，中间自动加箭头。

## 它解决什么

AI 做的 PPT，常见的毛病就这几样。

- 整页是一张图片，看着漂亮，错一个字也改不了
- 能编辑的又是一股模板味，谁做出来都长一个样
- 内容装不下就把字越缩越小，投到墙上看不清
- 美化的时候顺手把原文"润色"了，丢了一句都不知道
- 标题写成"数据分析""项目介绍"，只读标题串不成一个故事
- 每页字号忽大忽小，强调色到处都是
- 原稿里的公式、编号、来源说明，美化完就没了

这个 Skill 把这些都变成了脚本能检查的规矩，交付前先过一遍。

## 适合什么场景

- 口播视频、公众号文章配套的讲解 PPT
- 拿到一份朴素的工作汇报、课件、方案，想照某张图的风格整体换装
- 理科和教学课件，公式多、示意图多
- AI 工具教程，截图多
- 数据复盘、竞品分析，需要原生表格、图表和分析框架
- 会议室投影，需要更大的字号下限

## 工作原理

两条路线共用一套设计引擎，中间靠三份文件串起来。

```text
路线 A 美化 原稿.pptx ──解析──┐
 ├──> deck.json（每页内容） + style.json（风格） ──> plan.json（版式规划）
路线 B 生成 文章/题目 ──写稿──┘

plan.json ──> 出插画 ──> 组装原生 pptx ──> 渲染预览 ──> 自动检查 ──> 五维自评 ──> 交付
```

脚本负责确定性的活，Agent 负责理解内容和审美判断。

### 美化时少一个字，它都不交

原稿的每一段文字都会先存一份，美化完逐页核对。少一行字就报错，直接点名是哪一页、哪一句。

 

### 装不下的内容，写大纲时就拦住

每个版式都标了容量，比如漏斗最多 5 层、每层说明不超过 26 个字。超了就在大纲阶段提醒，排版时自动换一个装得下的版式。

 

### 出图以后，先给自己挑一遍刺

先查丢字、溢出、字压页脚、对比度、强调色用量这些硬伤，再把能数出来的证据列成表，从统一、层级、细节、传达、节奏五个方面给自己打分，要修的修完再交。

 

### 没装 LibreOffice 也能看图自检

预览默认用 LibreOffice 渲染。没装的话，它会按排版数据直接把每一页画出来，12 页大概 10 秒，左边是 LibreOffice，右边是近似画法。

 

### 没配生图模型也能用

背景、装饰和插画都有程序化的画法，上面所有的图都是在没接生图模型的情况下跑出来的。配了 OpenAI、Gemini、火山方舟或任意 OpenAI 兼容接口，插画会更丰富，单张失败会自动退回程序化插画。

## 安装

仓库根目录就是 skill 本身（`SKILL.md` 在最外层），装好之后第一次使用时，Skill 会自己检查环境、补装缺少的 Python 包。

### 方式一：让 Agent 自己装

在 Claude Code、Codex、Gemini CLI、Cursor 这类能执行命令的 Agent 里直接说：

```text
帮我安装这个 skill：https://github.com/zhouwei713/luobo-ppt
```

Agent 会把仓库克隆到它自己的 skills 目录。装完开一个新会话就能用。

### 方式二：一行命令克隆

把仓库克隆到你的 Agent 的 skills 目录，目录名用 `luobo-ppt`。

```bash
# Claude Code
git clone https://github.com/zhouwei713/luobo-ppt.git ~/.claude/skills/luobo-ppt

# Codex 及其他支持 SKILL.md 开放标准的 Agent
git clone https://github.com/zhouwei713/luobo-ppt.git ~/.agents/skills/luobo-ppt

# Gemini CLI
git clone https://github.com/zhouwei713/luobo-ppt.git ~/.gemini/skills/luobo-ppt

# Cursor
git clone https://github.com/zhouwei713/luobo-ppt.git ~/.cursor/skills/luobo-ppt
```

Windows 上 `~` 是 `C:\Users\你的用户名`。只想在某个项目里用，就克隆到项目里的 `.claude/skills/`、`.agents/skills/` 这类目录。

用 [skills CLI](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills) 的话，一行就行：

```bash
npx skills add zhouwei713/luobo-ppt
```

### 方式三：一键安装脚本

想一次装给电脑上所有的 Agent，并且提前把依赖装好：

```bash
git clone https://github.com/zhouwei713/luobo-ppt.git
cd luobo-ppt
bash install.sh
```

Windows 双击 `install.bat`，或在 PowerShell 里运行 `.\install.ps1`。脚本会自动找到装了哪些 Agent，分别装进去，检查并补装依赖，最后生成一份两页的小样做自测。只装给某一个 Agent 加参数就行，比如 `bash install.sh --agent codex`，更多参数见 [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md)。

### 方式四：Claude 应用

在仓库页面点 Code → Download ZIP，在 Claude 应用的技能设置里上传这个压缩包。

### 更新

```bash
cd ~/.claude/skills/luobo-ppt && git pull # 换成你实际的安装目录
```

### 依赖

| 类别 | 内容 |
|---|---|
| 必需 | Python 3.8+，python-pptx，Pillow，numpy，lxml，一款中文字体 |
| 推荐 | LibreOffice（预览更准），pdftoppm 或 PyMuPDF，requests（调用生图接口） |
| 可选 | 生图模型配置，见 `config.example.json` 和 `references/imagegen_config.md` |

`python3 scripts/setup_check.py --install` 会检查并安装缺少的部分。

## 使用方式

装好以后，跟 Agent 这么说：

```text
把这篇文章做成 12 页的口播 PPT，每页带口播备注，用墨水杂志风格。
```

```text
帮我美化这份 PPT，照着这张参考图的风格来，文字一个字都别改。
```

```text
这份数学课件帮我美化一下，公式都要保留。
```

```text
这是一篇工具教程，里面的截图帮我用截图版式排，操作点在截图上标出来。
```

```text
主题是"AI 工具号年度复盘"，给我出三张风格样张，我挑一个再往下做。
```

```text
这份 PPT 要在会议室投影，用投影模式，字号大一点。
```

赶时间可以加一句"快速模式"，它会跳过中间的确认环节。

## 14 套风格

没有参考图时，可以直接报名字。

 

| 风格 | 英文名 | 适合 |
|---|---|---|
| 薄荷清新 | mint-fresh | 科普讲解、工具教程、环保生活、小白入门 |
| 商务蓝 | business-blue | 工作汇报、方案提案、B 端产品、培训 |
| 暖橙活力 | warm-orange | 个人分享、活动宣传、营销增长、生活方式 |
| 深色科技 | dark-tech | AI 与科技产品、发布会、开发者内容 |
| 雾紫柔和 | lavender-soft | 情绪心理、美妆穿搭、读书感悟 |
| 纸感手记 | paper-notes | 读书笔记、方法论、个人成长、知识分享 |
| 黑金述职 | black-gold | 晋升述职、高层汇报、年度总结、高端品牌 |
| 几何色块 | geo-blocks | 运营复盘、团队年终、数据报告、市场活动 |
| 钴蓝字体 | cobalt-type | 设计分享、观点演讲、学术报告、创意提案 |
| 黑灰荧绿 | ink-lime | 业绩汇报、销售复盘、指标分析、项目进度 |
| 蓝粉柔雾 | pastel-mist | 实习汇报、校园分享、个人总结、轻量课程 |
| 蓝线发布 | wave-launch | 新品发布、科技大会、产品路线图、融资路演 |
| 墨水杂志 | ink-magazine | 观点分享、读书与人文、研究报告、个人品牌 |
| 硬边网格 | swiss-grid | 产品发布、方法论、数据复盘、设计提案 |

## 仓库结构

```text
.
├── SKILL.md Skill 主说明，Agent 读这个
├── INSTALL.md 安装说明
├── install.sh / install.ps1 / install.bat
├── config.example.json 生图模型配置模板
├── scripts/ 解析、规划、组装、渲染、检查、自评的全部脚本
├── references/ 版式库、deck.json 字段、风格提取、14 套风格预设、自评规则
├── assets/ 图标库、风格样张
└── docs/images/ README 用图
```

## 设计理念

好看的 PPT 少有靠堆装饰撑起来的。它先要讲得清楚：只读标题能串成一个故事，每页字数装得下，字号就那么几级，强调色只给最关键的那一处。

AI 最容易偷懒的地方恰好是这些看不见的规矩。所以这个 Skill 把它们写成了能数出来的检查，丢字、溢出、字号乱、对比度不够，脚本先过一遍，再让 AI 看图挑刺。

交出去的永远是原生 PPT。不满意的地方你自己动两下就行，不用求着 AI 重新生成。

## 致谢

做这个 Skill 时参考过这些项目和资料，全部只提炼思路、自己改写，没有搬运原文和代码。

- dashi-ppt-skill：给每个版式标注容量的思路

storytold/craft-fonts.text:
craft-fonts

Reusable fonts for the Crafting Apps.

This library is meant to have the following:

1. Reusable font assets. These may be large files, and since we're using a separate repo for storing them,
 We're not afraid of potentially having to do a git reset to purge stale assets. It won't impact the other
 repos with core app and library functionality.

2. Additional cross-cutting Rust libraries for dealing with fonts. It's uncertain whether it's better to
 have code packages as individual repos as one classically does, or whether we should take a
 more "biology-inspired" approach of copying innovations between repos as a form of lateral code/information
 exchange.

## What's here

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `fonts/` | The font files, one directory per family, each with its licence. |
| `fonts/manifest.txt` | Machine-readable list of every font: family, style, file, scripts, licence, SHA-256, pinned source. |
| `ATTRIBUTION.md` | Authors, pinned sources and licences. |
| `crates/craft-fonts` | Rust: the manifest as a static table, finding a checkout (`CRAFT_FONTS_DIR`), loading it, and an `embed` feature that compiles the fonts in. |
| `crates/craft-fonts-tests` | Tests asserted on these fonts: checksums, licences, family names, Japanese coverage and outlines, vertical-text (`vert`/`vrt2`) support. |
| `docs/integration.md` | How an app uses craft-fonts as a fully optional build input. |

### Fonts

| Family | Styles | For | Licence |
|---|---|---|---|
| BIZ UDPGothic | Regular, Bold | Japanese UI text (sans) | OFL-1.1 |
| Shippori Mincho | Regular | Japanese document text (serif) | OFL-1.1 |
| BIZ UDMincho | Regular | Japanese document text (serif) | OFL-1.1 |
| Noto Sans CJK SC | Regular | Simplified Chinese UI and document text (sans) | OFL-1.1 |
| Noto Sans Arabic | Regular (variable: wdth, wght) | Arabic UI and document text (sans) | OFL-1.1 |
| Noto Sans Thai | Regular (variable: wdth, wght) | Thai UI and document text (sans) | OFL-1.1 |

## How the apps use it

**Fully optional, never required.** The apps don't list craft-fonts in `Cargo.toml` (Cargo would
fetch it for every build). Building with `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR= ` makes an app
embed the fonts in `fonts/manifest.txt`; without it, the app builds and runs as before. Release
builds check out a pinned commit of this repo and set the option. See
[`docs/integration.md`](docs/integration.md).

**Font assets for the Crafting Apps belong here**, not in the app repos: add the file, its licence,
a manifest line and an attribution row, and the tests check it.

## Develop

```sh
cargo test --workspace # all font assertions
cargo test -p craft-fonts --features embed # the embedded bytes match the files
```

Code is MIT OR Apache-2.0 (`LICENSE-MIT`, `LICENSE-APACHE`); each font keeps its own licence.

aindeev/agent-chrome-relay.text:
# Chrome Relay

 
 
 
 
 
 
 

**Website:** https://agent-chrome-relay.aindeev.com

Lets your coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Paseo) use **your everyday Chrome**, with your real
logins, from the command line, **in background tabs**: nothing takes focus, no dialogs, ~0.15s per command.

```bash
agent-browser --cdp "$(chrome-relay url you@company.com)" open https://app.example.com/
agent-browser snapshot -i # the page's buttons, links and fields, each with a ref like @e5
agent-browser click @e5
agent-browser close
```

It's opt-in: nothing installs the extension for you, and it only runs on Macs whose owner set it up.

**The core** is background tabs with your logins, Google sign-in hops and an audit trail. **Everything else is
optional** and off until you turn it on: signing in with 1Password (passwords, 2-step codes, passkeys) and
Secure Enclave passkeys. See [What's optional](#whats-optional).

## How it works

```
agent-browser (CLI) ──ws──▶ relay (127.0.0.1:9333, LaunchAgent) ──ws──▶ Chrome Relay extension ──chrome.debugger──▶ agent tab
```

- **Extension** (`extension/`, MV3, one per Chrome profile you load it in): opens each agent tab **inactive**
 in a collapsed "Agents" tab group and runs DevTools commands in it via `chrome.debugger`. No remote-debugging
 port, so Chrome never shows "Allow remote debugging?". Chrome does show "Chrome Relay started debugging this
 browser" while agents work.
- **`chrome-relay`**: one Go program, **built and signed on your own Mac** (`./build`). As a background service
 (`chrome-relay serve`) it is the relay: a DevTools endpoint per agent, where each agent sees and controls only
 the tabs it opened and commands that could raise or focus the browser are swallowed. It is also the CLI
 (setup, the connection URL, diagnostics, audit trail), and the optional 1Password vault and passkeys, whose
 Secure Enclave and Touch ID code (`internal/macos`, Swift) is linked into the same signed binary when Xcode's
 command line tools are installed.

## Setup (once per Mac, ~2 minutes)

Fastest: paste [this prompt](https://agent-chrome-relay.aindeev.com/setup-prompt.txt) into Claude Code, Codex or
Cursor and let your agent do it. By hand:

Needs macOS, Google Chrome, [Go](https://go.dev/dl/) 1.25+ (`brew install go`) and
[`agent-browser`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-browser) (`npm i -g agent-browser`).

```bash
git clone https://github.com/aindeev/agent-chrome-relay
cd agent-chrome-relay
./build # compiles chrome-relay and signs it on this Mac (see below)
./chrome-relay setup # secret, background service, identities, `chrome-relay` on PATH, Claude Code skill
```

**Why you build it yourself**: the binary is signed on your Mac, and macOS ties Chrome Relay's Keychain item to
that signature, so only your own build can read it (see the 1Password section). The build uses the hardened
runtime, so other programs can't attach a debugger to the relay or inject code into it. Two things make the
build fuller, and neither is required:

| You have | `./build` makes | |
|---|---|---|
| Go only | the **core**: tabs, Google sign-in hops, audit trail | passkeys you keep in 1Password still work (1Password's prompt) |
| + Xcode's command line tools (`xcode-select --install`) | the core **plus 1Password and Secure Enclave passkeys** | |
| + a code signing identity | the same, **signed by you** | without one it signs ad-hoc: macOS may ask once after each rebuild before Chrome Relay reads its own Keychain item |

Any Apple Development or Developer ID certificate is an identity (`security find-identity -v -p codesigning`
lists yours; a free one comes with an Apple ID in Xcode → Settings → Accounts → Manage Certificates). With
several, pick one with `./build --identity " "`; it's remembered. `chrome-relay doctor` says which build
you have.

Then, **in each Chrome profile agents should use**: open `chrome://extensions`, turn on **Developer mode**,
**Load unpacked**, pick the `extension` folder of your clone, and **pin** it (puzzle-piece icon → pin) so you see its badge. Check with `chrome-relay doctor`.

After `git pull`: `./build && chrome-relay update` (rebuilds, restarts the relay, reloads the extension in every
profile).
To remove: `chrome-relay uninstall`, then remove the extension in each profile.

## Telling your agents

Claude Code: `setup` links the skill (`skill/SKILL.md`) into `~/.claude/skills/chrome-relay`, so every
repo gets it. Codex, Cursor and others: point them at the same file, e.g. a line in your global
`~/.codex/AGENTS.md`: *"For any browser step that needs my logins, follow
` /agent-chrome-relay/skill/SKILL.md`."* A repo's `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` only needs a
one-line pointer to the skill.

## Who can drive it

Two checks on every agent connection:

1. **This Mac's secret**: generated at setup in `~/.chrome-relay/token` (mode 600) and embedded in the URL
 that `chrome-relay url` prints.
2. **An allowed agent app**: the connecting process must come from Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or Paseo. The
 relay looks the process up (`lsof`, `ps`) and checks the markers those apps set in their child processes
 (`CLAUDECODE`, `CODEX_*`, `CURSOR_*`, `PASEO_AGENT_ID`), then its parent processes.

Connections that carry a browser `Origin` header (a web page) are refused even with the secret. Only **this
checkout's extension** may connect as the extension: Chrome derives an unpacked extension's ID from its folder,
`setup` records that ID in `~/.chrome-relay/config.json`, the relay checks the connection's
`Origin: chrome-extension:// ` (which pages cannot fake), and the connecting process must be Chrome.

This keeps other local tools, web pages and accidents out. It is not a boundary against malware already
running as you, which could read the secret and fake the markers.

## Sign-ins

Agents never type credentials they know. When a site bounces through Google and the right account is **already signed
in**, the extension clicks the account and **Continue/Allow** itself

fayazara/robot-heads.text:
# robot-heads

Animated 3D robot heads for React. Glossy, TV-headed bots with an LED-matrix face that shows what your agent is doing — thinking, searching, listening, speaking and more — in four shapes, with a springy antenna, knob ears and a light on top that changes with the state.

Drawn on a 2D canvas: no WebGL, no runtime dependencies.

**[Playground →](https://robot-heads.fayaz.workers.dev)**

## Install

```bash
npm install robot-heads
```

React 18 or newer is a peer dependency.

## Quick start

```tsx
import { RobotHead } from 'robot-heads';

function Agent({ status }: { status: 'idle' | 'thinking' | 'speaking' }) {
 return ;
}
```

## Shapes

One head, four outlines. Every shape carries the same screen, ears, antenna, screws and back panel, and moves the same way.

```tsx
 {/* the classic TV (default) */}
 
 {/* a porthole */}
 {/* a nut, flat on top */}
```

The list is exported as `robotHeadShapes`.

## States

Each state has its own face on the screen, its own motion and its own antenna light. Switching states plays a short glitch and cross-fade, and the head eases into its new pose.

| State | Screen | Motion |
|---|---|---|
| `idle` | block eyes that blink and glance | looks around, hops now and then |
| `thinking` | heavy-lidded eyes looking up, three pulsing dots | head tilted up, switching sides; amber light pulses |
| `searching` | darting eyes, a beam sweeping the whole screen | head sweeps side to side; cyan beacon |
| `listening` | alert eyes over a live equaliser | head cocked, small nods; steady green light |
| `speaking` | a mouth that moves with the words | bobs as it talks |
| `working` | focused eyes looking down, a progress bar | busy bobbing, a hop with a spin now and then |
| `happy` | `^ ^` eyes and a smile | bouncy hops |
| `error` | red `X X` eyes | shakes its head; red light blinks |
| `sleeping` | closed eyes and rising z's | head drooped, slow breathing; light off |

The list is exported as `robotHeadStates`.

## Props

```tsx
 
```

Any other attribute (`className`, `style`, `onClick`, `aria-label`, …) goes on the element, and a `ref` reaches the ` ` inside it.

## Sizing and layout

`size` is the robot itself: the element is a `size` × `size` box with the robot at rest centred in it, filling it, antenna included. It lines up with text, sits in a flex row, and centres like an icon or an avatar would.

Its motion is not part of that box. Hops, the antenna's glow and the floor's shadow draw past its edges — like a CSS `box-shadow`, they overflow without taking any room in your layout, and only the box takes clicks. So margins, flex and grid treat it as exactly `size` × `size`; the one thing to watch is a parent with `overflow: hidden` right round it, which would cut off a hop.

## Behaviour

- **Pointer play.** With `interactive` on (the default), the head and eyes follow a nearby pointer, and a click makes it hop with a full spin and a happy face.
- **Small sizes.** For avatars in a list, `antenna={false}` drops the antenna's stem and its light, keeping the knob on top, so the head itself fills more of the box (the square, circle and hexagon grow; the wide rectangle is already as big as its width allows).
- **Reduced motion.** With `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, or `paused`, the still pose of the state is drawn instead of the animation.
- **Accessible by default.** The canvas has `role="img"` and an `aria-label` naming the state ("Robot, thinking"); pass your own `aria-label` to override it.
- **Cheap to run many.** Every head on the page shares one animation loop, which sleeps while the tab is hidden, and heads of the same shape and size share their baked textures.

## How it is drawn

The head is real geometry: a shell with a rolled edge — its outline a convex polygon of corner centres grown by a corner radius, so one builder makes every shape — lathed knob ears and an antenna collar, built once as quad meshes. Each frame it is turned with the pose and projected, back faces are culled, and every quad is lit by a small studio model: a key light, a fill, a sky dome, a softbox and the key's window caught as clear-coat reflections with Fresnel, a cool back light rimming the silhouette, and a filmic tone curve.

The flat front and back are plates drawn in their own plane with baked relief: the lip rolling into the screen hole, the rubber gasket, the shadow the lip casts onto the glass, screws, and vents on the back. The glass sits a little behind the bezel, so it slides against it as the head turns. The LED matrix covers the whole screen, the face centred on it; the LEDs are drawn crisp, then bloomed from a one-pixel-per-LED image scaled up smooth. The antenna is a damped spring that whips when the head hops, lands or tilts, topped with a frosted bulb lit from inside.

## Development

The repo is a pnpm workspace: the library at the root, the playground in `site/` — a React app on [Vite](https://vite.dev) served by a [Cloudflare Worker](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/). The playground runs on the library's source, so edits hot-reload there.

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm run dev # the playground
pnpm run build # the library, to dist/
pnpm run typecheck
pnpm run deploy # build and deploy the playground Worker
```

```
src/ the library
 RobotHead.tsx the component
 tv/ the TV head: geometry, lighting, faces, motion, renderer
site/ the playground (Vite + Cloudflare Worker)
```

## License

[MIT](LICENSE) © [Fayaz Ahmed](https://x.com/fayazara)

The playground is set in [Open Runde](https://github.com/lauridskern/open-runde) by Laurids Kern, under the SIL Open Font License 1.1 (`site/public/fonts/OFL.txt`). The font is not part of the npm package.

nikgrbn/finder-menu.text:
Finder Menu 

 
 The right-click options macOS is missing. 
 New File, Open Terminal Here, Open Folder With, Copy Path and Go to Parent Folder, in Finder's own menu.
 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
 Install ·
 What's in the menu ·
 Templates ·
 Settings ·
 Languages ·
 Privacy ·
 How it works 
 

 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 Right-click empty space in any folder. Finder's own items are faded here to show what Finder Menu adds. 
 

 

 
 
 📂 Built-in Five actions in Finder's own right-click menu. 
 🧰 Your tools Terminals, VS Code, Cursor, JetBrains, Xcode… 
 🔒 Private No network code, no telemetry. 
 🪶 Tiny About 900 lines of Swift, built on your Mac. 
 
 

## What's in the menu

Right-click **empty space** in any folder, with nothing selected:

|        | Menu item | What it does |
|:-:|---|---|
| | **New File…** | Asks for a name with any extension (`notes.md`, `main.py`, `.env`), creates it in the current folder and selects it. Never overwrites. Names you use often can be [saved as templates](#new-file-templates). |
| | **Open Terminal Here** | Opens a terminal in the current folder: iTerm2, Ghostty, Warp, WezTerm, kitty or Alacritty if you have one, otherwise Terminal. [Pick your own](#settings). |
| | **Open Folder With ▸** | Opens the current folder in an IDE or editor. Lists the ones you have installed (VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Zed, Sublime Text, JetBrains IDEs, Android Studio, Xcode…), plus **Other App…** to pick any app. |
| | **Copy Path** | Copies the current folder's full path. |
| | **Go to Parent Folder** | Moves the window up one level, even when Finder's Back button is greyed out (e.g. a window opened with `open .`). |

Right-clicking a file or folder works too: **Copy Path** copies the selected items' paths, and **Open Terminal Here** and **Open Folder With** use the selected folder.

The menu also appears on external drives, disk images and network shares (such as SMB), not just your Mac's own disk.

## New File templates

 
 
 
 
 
 

1. Tick **Save as template** in the New File dialog.
2. Next time, pick it under **New File** to create an empty `notes.md` in one click.

If the name is taken, you get `notes 2.md`, like in Finder. **Manage Templates…** removes templates.

## Install

**With Homebrew:**

```bash
brew install nikgrbn/tap/finder-menu
finder-menu enable
```

**Or from source:**

```bash
git clone https://github.com/nikgrbn/finder-menu.git
cd finder-menu
./install.sh
```

Either way, the app is built on your machine, installed to `~/Applications/Finder Menu.app` and the Finder extension is turned on. There's nothing to launch: Finder loads the extension by itself, including after a restart.

> [!NOTE]
> The first time you use **Go to Parent Folder**, macOS asks whether Finder Menu can control Finder. Click **OK**, because that's how it moves the window.

### Update

```bash
brew update && brew upgrade finder-menu
finder-menu enable
```

From source, run `git pull && ./install.sh` in the repo folder.

> [!TIP]
> Don't skip `brew update`: on its own, `brew upgrade` checks for new versions only once a day.

## Settings

Open **Finder Menu** from Spotlight or your Applications folder, or run `finder-menu settings`. The settings window lets you:

- choose which items appear in the right-click menu
- choose whether the menu also appears on external and network drives (it does by default)
- pick the terminal for **Open Terminal Here**. Automatic uses the first one installed, in this order: iTerm2, Ghostty, Warp, WezTerm, kitty, Alacritty, Terminal. **Other App…** lets you pick any app.
- remove [New File templates](#new-file-templates)

 
 
 
 
 
 

Changes apply the next time you right-click. You can also set the terminal from the command line: `finder-menu terminal Ghostty` (any app name works), `finder-menu terminal` to see the current choice, and `finder-menu terminal auto` to go back to automatic. If you installed from source, run `scripts/finder-menu` from the repo folder instead.

## Languages

Finder Menu uses your Mac's language:

- 🇺🇸 English
- 🇩🇪 German, translated by [@9trzj5nztr-design](https://github.com/9trzj5nztr-design)
- 🇮🇹 Italian
- 🇷🇺 Russian
- 🇺🇦 Ukrainian, translated by [@artemartemenko](https://github.com/artemartemenko)

Any other language falls back to English. Want yours? See [Contributing](#contributing).

## Uninstall

With Homebrew:

```bash
finder-menu disable
brew uninstall finder-menu
```

From source:

```bash
./uninstall.sh
```

## Troubleshooting

- **Menu items don't appear:** hold ⌥, right-click Finder in the Dock and choose **Relaunch**. Also check that **Finder Menu** is turned on under System Settings → General → Login Items & Extensions → Finder extensions.
- **Asked for permission again after reinstalling:** expected. Every build is signed locally with a new signature, so macOS asks again.
- **A drive shows the Finder Menu icon in Finder's sidebar:** some macOS versions give the drives a Finder extension works on that app's icon. It's only the icon. If it bothers you, untick **Also on external and network drives** in [settings](#settings), which also takes the menu off those drives.

## How it works

- `Sources/FinderMenuExtension` is a [Finder Sync extension](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/findersync) that adds the menu items to every folder. Finder only asks it about the drives it lists, so it lists every mounted drive and updates the list when one is mounted or ejected. Finder extensions must run sandboxed, so this part only reads the clicked folder and copies paths.
- `Sources/FinderMenu` is a small helper app that isn't sandboxed and has no Dock icon. The extension hands it actions through a `findermenu://` URL, and the helper ignores those URLs from anything else. It creates the files, opens the terminal and moves the Finder window, then quits.
- `Sources/Shared/Settings.swift` holds the list of menu items and reads the settings; `Sources/FinderMenu/

finnvoor/PiDurableKit.text:
# PiDurableKit

Durable AI agents for iPhone, iPad, Mac, and Vision Pro, powered by [`@earendil-works/pi-durable`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@earendil-works/pi-durable) running in JavaScriptCore.

Conversations, model turns, tool calls, and your own state are committed to storage before anything is shown. If iOS kills your app mid-turn, reopening the storage picks the work up where it stopped.

```swift
import PiDurableKit

let models = Models(credentials: .keychain)
try await models.setAPIKey(anthropicKey, for: .anthropic)
let harness = try await Harness.open(.sqlite(at: .documentsDirectory.appending(path: "agent.sqlite")), models: models)
let root = try await harness.root(agent: AgentChange(model: .anthropic("claude-sonnet-4-5")))

let submission = try await root.submit("What is the capital of France?")
let settled = try await submission.wait()
if case .done(_, let answer?) = settled.status {
 let entry = try await root.commit { tx in try await tx.entry(answer) }
 print(entry?.assistantMessage?.text ?? "")
}
```

- Swift tools, system prompt sections, hooks, and wraps, written as plain closures
- Subagents, durable tasks with child tasks, and atomic transactions
- Every pi-ai provider (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, OpenRouter, Groq, xAI, Mistral, …) plus any OpenAI- or Anthropic-compatible server
- SQLite or JSONL persistence with crash recovery, or in-memory storage
- pi-durable's `read`/`write`/`edit` tools in a sandboxed directory
- Streaming: `AsyncSequence`s of conversation views (for SwiftUI) and coding-agent style events
- Steering, follow-ups, abort, reset, compaction, forks, typed documents and entries, usage and cost
- OAuth sign-in to Claude Pro/Max, ChatGPT, GitHub Copilot, and OpenRouter, with tokens in the Keychain and automatic refresh
- A scripted faux provider for tests and SwiftUI previews

Requires iOS 17, macOS 14, tvOS 17, or visionOS 1.

## Installation

```swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/ /PiDurableKit.git", from: "1.0.0")
```

and add `PiDurableKit` to your target's dependencies.

## Concepts

The Swift API mirrors pi-durable's, with Swift concurrency in place of Chord contexts (cancel the Swift task to cancel a wait; cancelling a wait never cancels the work).

| pi-durable | PiDurableKit |
|---|---|
| `createModels({ credentials })` + providers | `Models(credentials:)`, `models.register(CustomProvider(…))` |
| `Harness.open(storage, { models, registry, settings })` | `Harness.open(.sqlite(at:), models:, extensions:, settings:)` |
| `harness.root()`, `createConversation()`, `fork()` | `harness.root(agent:)`, `harness.createConversation(ownedBy:agent:)`, `conversation.fork(at:ownedBy:)` |
| `tx.scanConversations()`, `tx.conversation()`, `tx.entry()` | `harness.conversations(ownedBy:)`, `conversation.record()`, `conversation.entry(_:)` |
| `conversation.submit({ type: "input", … })` | `conversation.submit("…", whenBusy:, requestId:)` |
| `conversation.submit({ type: "write", … })` | `conversation.write(EntryDraft(…))` |
| `submission.wait()`, `tx.entry(AssistantEntry, id)` | `submission.wait()`, `tx.entry(id)?.assistantMessage` |
| `harness.submission(id)`, `abortSubmission(id, context, conversationId)` | `harness.submission(_:)`, `harness.abortSubmission(_:in:)` |
| `conversation.context({ at })` → `head`, `entries`, `contributions`, `messages` | `conversation.context(at:)` → `ContextView` |
| `EntryDraft.head`, `EntryDraft.edits` (`ContextEdit`) | `EntryDraft(kind:head: .itself / .entry(id), edits: [.omit(id), .replace(id, with:)])` |
| `conversation.configure(change)` | `conversation.configure(AgentChange(…))` |
| `defineExtension`, `defineTool`, `section`, `hook` | `Extension`, `Tool`, `PromptSection`, `Hook` |
| `wrapTool`, `wrapSection` | `Wrap.tool(_:definition:prepareArguments:execute:)`, `Wrap.section` |
| `hook(GenerationTask, { onYield })` with user content | `Hook.onYield` (text), `Hook.onYieldContent` (text and images) |
| an extension written in JavaScript | `Extension(name, javaScript: source)` |
| `defineTask`, `TaskRuntime` | `TaskType`, `Phase`, `TaskRun` |
| `harness.commit()`, `conversation.commit()`, `Tx` | `harness.commit { tx in … }`, `conversation.commit { tx in … }`, `Transaction` |
| `ToolExecutionApi` (`commit`, `conversation`, `memo`, `env`, `registry`, `outputWindow`, …) | `ToolCallContext` (`environment()`, `registry()`, `outputWindow`, `output(_:skipped:)`, …) |
| `TaskRuntime` `env()`, `settings`, `registry` | `run.environment()`, `run.settings()`, `run.registry()` |
| `registry.snapshot()`, `resolveSettings()`, `DEFAULT_*_POLICY` | `harness.registry()`, `harness.resolvedSettings()`, `Runtime.defaultSettings()` |
| `conversation.watch()` / `viewState()` | `conversation.changes()` / `conversation.views()`, `conversation.view()` |
| `watchEvents(harness, id)` → `snapshot`, `start(listener)` | `harness.watchEvents(id)` → `snapshot`, `for try await events in stream` |

## A Simple Harness Outperforms VLA and World Action Models

**[Project Page](https://bincequ.github.io/RoboHarness/) · [Quick Start](#run-a-task) · [Documentation](docs/setup.md) · [中文](README.zh-CN.md)**

 

 

 RoboHarness overview: visual keypoints are tracked persistently, converted into geometric constraints, executed, and verified in a closed loop. [View original PDF](docs/assets/overview.pdf) 

 

## Overview

Without training models, RoboHarness combines visual clicks, keypoint tracking,
and geometric constraints to provide an embodied control panel for an LLM agent.

The LLM marks points of interest on a 2D image and continuously receives their
positions via optical-flow tracking and depth back-projection; with this
information, it composes accurate primitive actions to perform complex
manipulation.

The reported BEHAVIOR results use Claude Code 2.1.259 with
`Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8` and the R1 Pro robot. A Codex harness is also available.

## What is included

| Component | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`BEHAVIOR/`](BEHAVIOR) | BEHAVIOR simulator and evaluator, pinned to v3.9.1 |
| [`interface/`](interface) | RGB-D observations, robot control and interactive interface |
| [`harness/claude_code/`](harness/claude_code) | Claude Code harness |
| [`harness/codex/`](harness/codex) | Codex harness |
| [`prompt/`](prompt) | Task-specific instructions for household manipulation |
| [`tasks/`](tasks) | Task definitions, evaluation instances and step budgets |
| [`reference_results/`](reference_results) | Reference evaluator scores |
| [`roboharness/`](roboharness) | Task runner and evaluation pipeline |
| [`validation_results/`](validation_results) | Evaluation reports and scores |

## Installation

Use Linux x86-64, an NVIDIA RTX GPU, Python 3.11 and the CUDA 12.4 toolkit.
The validation host has 48 GB VRAM per GPU; this is the tested capacity, not a
measured minimum. You also need BEHAVIOR scene data, local cache space and a
separately configured model endpoint.

```bash
git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/BinceQu/RoboHarness.git
cd RoboHarness
./scripts/setup.sh
cp configs/example.json configs/local.json
```

Follow the [installation guide](docs/setup.md) to obtain the licensed datasets,
install Claude Code 2.1.259, and configure the model endpoint and authentication.
Edit `configs/local.json` for this machine's data and Python paths.

## Run a task

The model server and the evaluation runner are separate processes. Keep your
model server running throughout evaluation. `setup.sh` installs the simulation
and agent environments; it does not download LLM weights or start a model server.

**1. Connect to your model service.**

The default Claude Code harness uses an **Anthropic-compatible `/v1/messages`
endpoint with image input, tool calls and streaming**. The paper configuration
uses `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8`. If your server only provides OpenAI Chat
Completions, follow the [bridge setup](docs/setup.md#chat-completions-services)
first. Codex uses a different [Responses configuration](docs/setup.md#codex-model-service).

On the **evaluation machine**, open a terminal in this repository and replace
the host, served model ID and key below with your service's values:

```bash
export ROBOHARNESS_MODEL_URL='http://YOUR_MODEL_HOST:31000'
export ROBOHARNESS_MODEL='Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8'
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY='YOUR_MODEL_SERVER_KEY'
export ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN="$ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"
```

Use the origin **without `/v1`** for `ROBOHARNESS_MODEL_URL`. The model ID must
match the name exposed by your server. For a server with authentication disabled,
use `local-no-auth` as the key. `127.0.0.1` works only when the model service is
on this evaluation machine, or an SSH tunnel forwards it here.

Send a small request before starting the simulator:

```bash
python3 - <<'PY' | curl --fail-with-body --silent --show-error \
 "${ROBOHARNESS_MODEL_URL%/}/v1/messages" \
 -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
 -H 'anthropic-version: 2023-06-01' \
 -H "x-api-key: $ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" \
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN" \
 --data-binary @-
import json, os
print(json.dumps({
 "model": os.environ["ROBOHARNESS_MODEL"], "max_tokens": 128,
 "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Reply with OK."}]
}))
PY
```

Expect a Messages response with `"type": "message"`. This checks reachability,
authentication and the model ID; the service must also support the image and
tool features above. Connection errors, HTTP 401/403 and HTTP 404 are covered in
[model connection troubleshooting](docs/setup.md#model-connection-troubleshooting).

**2. Save the session configuration.**

In the same terminal, copy your installation settings on first use and save
the model address and name. Existing session settings are retained:

```bash
python3 - <<'PY'
import json, os
from pathlib import Path
path = Path(os.environ.get("ROBOHARNESS_SESSION_CONFIG", ".local/session-config.json"))
source = path if path.exists() else Path("configs/local.json")
config = json.loads(source.read_text())
config.update(model_url=os.environ["ROBOHARNESS_MODEL_URL"],
 model=os.environ["ROBOHARNESS_MODEL"])
path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
path.write_text(json.dumps(config, indent=2) + "\n")
print("Saved", path)
PY
```

The default session file is `.local/session-config.json`; set
`ROBOHARNESS_SESSION_CONFIG` to select another file. Review it: `data_path` must point to the
[BEHAVIOR data root](docs/setup.md), and `interface_python`, `evaluator_python`
and `agent_python` must point to the installed environments. The example paths
work with `setup.sh`. Set `cache_dir` to writable scratch space outside any
Git checkout when needed. Relative paths are resolved from the repository root.
Credentials stay in the shell environment; export them again in each new
terminal. Later configuration edits belong in this session file.

**3. Inspect the plan, then launch.**

```bash
claude --version # must be 2.1.259 for the paper configuratio

CG Claude 把系统时区、终端环境、浏览器设置和 Claude Code 配置集中到一个桌面工作台。先检测问题、查看修改预览，再保存配置；需要回退时，可以恢复修改前的快照。

 

_实际应用界面，使用独立演示目录。截图中的配置与检测结果仅作示例。_

## 可以做什么

| 功能 | 使用方式 |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 环境检测 | 31 项检查，默认连续检测 3 遍。点击「需要关注」直接定位问题，展开查看证据、处理方法和来源。 |
| 一键配置 | 5 步向导先确认目标和修改范围，再预览执行。13 个节点依次处理，每个节点首次失败后最多重试 3 次；仍失败则继续下一项。 |
| 备份恢复 | 写入前自动备份并保存完整配置快照。可恢复单次修改，或预览后还原整份配置快照。 |
| 本机配置 | 编辑 Claude Code 的代理、API 地址、NO_PROXY 和额外 CA 路径；外部浏览器语言配置提供独立预览、保存与还原。 |
| 项目扫描 | 选择本地项目，核对 Claude 配置、权限、Hooks、MCP、TLS、凭据声明与锁文件。只读扫描，不执行项目脚本。 |
| 记录与依据 | 保留检测历史、导出报告、记录人工复核。内置原文对照与参考文献，可从检测项跳到对应来源。 |
| 翻译模型 | 配置 OpenAI 兼容或 Anthropic 接口，测试中译英、英译中。**当前尚未接入 Claude Code 原生会话。** |
| 应用设置 | 中英文界面、浅色／护眼／深色配色、减少动画、版本检查，以及菜单栏／系统托盘。打包的 macOS / Windows 版支持开机自启。 |

首页还提供 [LC-time 浏览器环境配置插件](https://github.com/LcodeCoder/LC-time) 入口，方便单独查看浏览器插件及安装说明。

## 安装

前往 [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/LcodeCoder/CG-Claude/releases) 选择已发布版本，下载与你的系统和 CPU 架构对应的附件。安装桌面版后，无需另外安装 Node.js。若发布页暂未提供安装包，可以先按下方「源码启动」运行。

当前版本为 **1.2.7**，安装包命名如下：

| 系统 | 安装包 | 安装方式 |
| --------------------- | --------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| macOS · Apple Silicon | `CG-Claude-1.2.7-macos-arm64.dmg` | 打开 DMG，将应用拖入「应用程序」。 |
| macOS · Intel | `CG-Claude-1.2.7-macos-x64.dmg` | 打开 DMG，将应用拖入「应用程序」。 |
| Windows · x64 | `CG-Claude-1.2.7-windows-x64-setup.exe` | 运行安装程序，按提示完成安装。 |
| Linux · x64 | `CG-Claude-1.2.7-linux-x86_64.AppImage` | 添加执行权限后直接运行。 |
| Debian / Ubuntu · x64 | `CG-Claude-1.2.7-linux-amd64.deb` | 使用系统软件安装器，或通过 `apt` 安装。 |

 
 Linux 启动命令与安装包校验 

AppImage：

```sh
chmod +x CG-Claude-1.2.7-linux-x86_64.AppImage
./CG-Claude-1.2.7-linux-x86_64.AppImage
```

Debian / Ubuntu：

```sh
sudo apt install ./CG-Claude-1.2.7-linux-amd64.deb
```

下载同一版本的 `SHA256SUMS.txt`，在安装包所在目录核对文件完整性：

```sh
shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS.txt
```

Windows PowerShell 可计算单个文件的校验值，与清单对照：

```powershell
Get-FileHash .\CG-Claude-1.2.7-windows-x64-setup.exe -Algorithm SHA256
```

 

macOS 安装包尚未签名、公证，Windows 安装包尚未进行发布者签名。Windows / Linux 的桌面交互尚未实机验证，已验证范围见 [交付记录](docs/release-1.2.7.md)。

### 源码启动

需要 **Node.js 22.12 或更新版本**：

```sh
git clone https://github.com/LcodeCoder/CG-Claude.git
cd CG-Claude
npm ci
npm run desktop
```

macOS 也可双击 `启动工具.command`，Windows 可双击 `启动工具.cmd`；首次运行需要安装依赖并构建应用。

## 第一次使用

1. **选择检测目标。** 在「检测偏好」设置实际使用的网络模式、服务方式与目标时区；也可以在「一键配置」中逐项选择。
2. **开始检测。** 默认连续检查 3 遍，仅读取本机配置。需要比较公网出口或 WebRTC 时，再勾选对应网络检测。
3. **查看并处理问题。** 点击顶部「需要关注」定位详情。自动修改先展示预览，确认后备份并执行。
4. **完成剩余设置。** 配置结束后查看手动清单，按步骤打开系统设置、复制核对命令或打开终端。重新打开终端与 Claude Code 后再次检测。
5. **需要时恢复。** 在「备份恢复」选择修改记录或完整快照，查看还原预览后恢复。

最小化或关闭桌面窗口后，应用留在菜单栏／系统托盘，检测与配置任务继续执行。需要完全退出时，从图标菜单选择「退出 CG Claude」。

## 应用截图

以下截图来自 **1.2.7 macOS 桌面版**，使用隔离演示数据；配置写入只作用于临时目录，系统时区使用模拟状态。点击展开查看完整界面。

 
 一键配置：逐项选择，先预览再执行 

向导依次确认网络模式、Claude 服务、隐私偏好与修改范围。系统时区可以按文章建议、当前 IP 出口或手动目标核对。

 

执行记录显示每个节点的结果和重试次数。配置完成后，仍需手动处理的事项集中列出，并提供设置入口与操作步骤。

 

 

 
 备份恢复：保留修改记录与完整配置快照 

可以查看单次修改的备份，或还原一键配置前的完整快照。还原前再次核对当前文件；有后续修改时会阻止覆盖，并在还原前保存当前状态。

 

 

 
 翻译模型：接口、模型、密钥与双向测试 

模型配置集中在「双向翻译」导航中。测试只发送两段固定示例，不读取项目或 Claude 会话；页面明确显示原生终端的接入状态。

 

 

 
 应用设置：深色模式与常用偏好 

提供中英文界面、浅色／护眼／深色配色、减少动画和版本检查。语言与外观保存在本机，重新打开后仍保留。

 

 

## 检测与数据范围

- **检测按实际配置与所选目标判断。** 环境检查不推算账号状态，也不保证账号安全；地区支持、登录设备、计费与账号事项需要人工核对。
- **浏览器有独立的检测对象。** CG 内置窗口的采样只代表当前窗口。用于登录的外部 Chrome、Edge、Firefox 或 Safari，需要选择对应资料或按提供的设置指引另外核对。
- **已有会话需要重新打开。** 修改启动文件不会更新已经打开的终端进程；系统时区、终端 TZ 与浏览器时区分别复检。
- **数据默认保存在本机。** 记录位于 `~/.claude-guard/`；备份与快照可能包含原配置中的凭据。界面隐藏密钥，报告导出默认进一步隐藏 IP 与主机名。
- **外部请求按操作发起。** 公网检测会连接出口查询服务；翻译测试连接你配置的模型服务；版本检查查询 GitHub。它们与本机只读检测分别开启。
- **项目扫描检查配置与元数据。** 完整源码审计、依赖漏洞分析和构建验证需要另行使用相应工具。

完整的写入规则、快照覆盖范围、网络访问与本机记录说明见 [检测与配置说明](docs/local-configuration.md)。

## 开发与文档

技术栈：Vue 3、TypeScript、Vite、Electron、Node.js 与 Zod。界面、共享类型、本机服务和桌面能力分别位于 `src/`、`shared/`、`server/`、`electron/`。

```sh
npm run check # 架构边界、类型与测试
npm run format:check # 格式检查
npm run pack # 生成应用目录
npm run dist # 生成当前平台安装包
```

 
 浏览器版、隔离演示与只读 CLI 

在已经运行 `npm ci` 的项目目录中：

```sh
npm run build
npm start
```

浏览器访问 `http://127.0.0.1:4318`。服务只监听回环地址，使用 Ctrl+C 退出。同一记录目录不能同时运行浏览器服务与桌面版。

```sh
npm run demo # 隔离浏览器演示，默认端口 4319
npm run desktop:demo # 隔离桌面演示
npm run doctor -- --json # 只读 CLI 检测
```

`demo` 在临时目录中创建示例配置，需先完成 `npm run build`。`desktop:demo` 自动构建，使用独立桌面资料目录。隔离模式不注册开机自启，系统时区与 TZ 使用模拟状态；平台信息及客户端版本仍按本机读取。CLI 加上 `--network` 可开启终端公网查询。

| 运行变量 | 用途 |
| ------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `CG_PORT` | 浏览器服务端口，默认 4318；桌面版使用随机回环端口。 |
| `CG_HOME` | 配置根目录，默认当前用户主目录；可用于隔离验证。 |
| `CG_DATA_DIR` | 记录目录，默认配置根目录下 `.claude-guard`。 |
| `CG_DEMO=1` | 标记隔离模式，应同时指定独立配置根目录。 |

 

| 文档 | 内容 |
| --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| [项目架构](docs/architecture.md) | 分层、代码入口、检查扩展与样式组织。 |
| [参与开发](CONTRIBUTING.md) | 本地验证、提交约定与改动要求。 |
| [检测与配置说明](docs/local-configuration.md) | 修复流程、配置范围、快照与本机数据。 |
| [原文逐项对照](docs/article-audit.md) | 43 项文章要求的检测、修复与人工核对映射。 |
| [参考文献审计](docs/reference-audit.md) | 69 条来源的采用内容与适用边界。 |
| [时区检测说明](docs/timezone-detection.md) | 系统、进程与浏览器时区的证据来源。 |
| [验证记录](docs/validation.md) | 各轮验收、实际测试与未覆盖范围。 |
| [发布说明](docs/publishing.md) | 多平台构建、校验值与 GitHub Release 流程。 |

安装包通过 GitHub Release 附件分发，源码仓库不提交二进制产物。`Check` 工作流验证三个系统；`Build installers` 在原生平台构建安装包并上传 Artifacts，正式 Release 由维护者发布。

[查看版本](https://github.com/LcodeCoder/CG-Claude/releases) · [报告问题](https://github.com/LcodeCoder/CG-Claude/issues) · [给项目一个 Star](https://github.com/LcodeCoder/CG-Claude)

## 社区与鸣谢

感谢 [LINUX DO](https://linux.do/) 提供技术交流与经验分享的平台，也感谢社区里乐于分享的佬友。

欢迎在 [LINUX DO 社区](https://linux.do/) 交流 CG Claude 的使用体验。遇到问题或有功能建议，也可以提交到 [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/LcodeCoder/CG-Claude/issues)。

# BetterWispr

**Free, open-source voice dictation for macOS.** Hold **⌥ Space**, speak, release, and the text lands in whatever app you were typing in.

BetterWispr is a private, offline speech-to-text app and an open-source alternative to Wispr Flow. It transcribes on your Mac with Whisper, NVIDIA Parakeet or Apple's on-device speech recognition, so your voice never leaves your computer unless you add an API connection yourself.

[Download the latest release](https://github.com/opennookorg/betterwispr/releases/latest) · [Website](https://betterwispr.com) · [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md)

 

## Features

- **Dictate anywhere**: hold-to-talk or press-to-toggle, with a shortcut you choose.
- **On-device models**: Apple speech, Parakeet v3 (25 European languages), Parakeet v2 (English) and Whisper large-v3 turbo.
- **Vocabulary**: spelling hints and phrase replacements for names and jargon.
- **Learns your corrections**: fix a misheard word once (in History, or right after it's pasted) and it's spelled right next time.
- **Voice commands**: say "comma", "new line", "scratch that" or "sorry, remove that", and "at the rate KV" for "@KV".
- **Meetings**: live transcript of you and the other side, plus on-device titles, summaries and action items with Apple Intelligence or a local Ollama model.
- **History**: raw and corrected transcripts, stored locally (can be turned off).
- **Bring your own model**: optional Sarvam AI, Smallest AI or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

## Requirements

- macOS 14 or later
- Apple Silicon recommended

## Getting started

1. Download the DMG from [Releases](https://github.com/opennookorg/betterwispr/releases/latest) and drag BetterWispr to Applications.
2. Open it and follow the welcome guide.
3. Pick a model in **Models**. Apple on-device needs no download; Parakeet and Whisper download once, then work offline.
4. Grant **Microphone** access, and **Accessibility** access so BetterWispr can paste for you.
5. Click into a text field in any app, hold **⌥ Space**, speak, and release.

If paste can't safely reach the previous app, the text is copied to your
clipboard instead, so you never lose a dictation. Recordings stop automatically
after two minutes.

## Bring your own model

**Models → Bring your own model → Add connection.** Choose a provider, enter the
model ID and API key, save, then click **Use**.

| Provider | Default model | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sarvam AI | `saaras:v4` | Long recordings are sent in 25-second chunks |
| Smallest AI | `pulse` | Set an explicit spoken language in Settings |
| OpenAI-compatible | any | Full URL, e.g. `http://localhost:8000/v1/audio/transcriptions`. HTTPS required except on localhost |

When a connection is in use, your audio goes to that endpoint and its pricing
and retention policies apply. Keys are stored in the macOS Keychain. Switch back
to a built-in model to return to fully local transcription. BetterWispr never
falls back to a cloud provider on its own.

## Privacy

- Settings, vocabulary and history live in `~/Library/Application Support/BetterWispr/workspace.json` (not encrypted).
- Models live in the `Models` folder next to it.
- Audio is written to temporary files and deleted after each recording.
- Built-in models only touch the network when you explicitly download one.

## Troubleshooting

- **Paste stopped working after an update or rebuild**: remove and re-add BetterWispr in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility.
- **Apple on-device model unavailable**: your language or OS speech assets may not support it. Install Parakeet or Whisper instead.
- **First transcription is slow**: large models take time to load the first time.

## Contributing

Build instructions, project layout and guidelines are in [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md).

## License

[Apache-2.0](LICENSE). Third-party code and model weights keep their own terms;

# 失业了咋办？Andy 给你保姆级攻略

**How to Survive Unemployment｜一份给普通人的免费开源失业自救指南**

失业前 · 前 7 天 · 3 个月 · 6 个月 · 1 年

**N / N+1 / 2N · 失业金 · 社保医保 · 公积金 · 找工作 · 个人生意 · 家庭现金流**

 

[**打开在线互动指南**](https://aipmandy.github.io/how-to-survive-unemployment/) · [**从这里开始，3分钟分流**](https://aipmandy.github.io/how-to-survive-unemployment/guides/00-start-here.html) · [开始：失业后 7 天](#先做这-7-件事) · [北京政策](guides/beijing.md) · [上海政策](guides/shanghai.md) · [现金流模板](templates/cashflow.md) · [参与共建](CONTRIBUTING.md)

> **遇到裁员，先别急着签字。** 如果已经失业，先核对补偿、失业金和医保，再算你手上的现金还能覆盖几个月。后面的选择，才有判断基础。
>
> 本项目免费、无须登录，政策最后核验：**2026-10-08**。适用资格、金额和办理流程以**经办时**的官方最新政策和个人情况为准。本项目不提供针对个人的法律、财税或保险意见。
> 信息反馈和咨询请联系微信 **AIPMAndy** · [Andy 官网](https://metaver.vip/)。作者咨询为可选服务，不影响免费使用指南。

## 这个仓库解决什么问题？

前段时间，有位朋友从 100 公里外专门来找我吃饭。他在公司待了 6 年，知道自己要拿 N+1，却不知道离开以后怎么办。

我平时会帮很多社招朋友做求职咨询。失业后的问题，往往不止找工作：补偿怎么谈、医保是否会断、失业金在哪领、什么时候可以转去做自己的生意？

所以做了这份指南。**所有建议都尽量落到具体行动，政策附原文，读者可以自己核对。**

### 先做这 7 件事

1. **没离职：** 确认解除原因，核对 N / N+1 / 2N，**别把不符合事实的“主动辞职”签成定案**。
2. **当天：** 核对离职证明、补偿金额、付款日期、欠付工资、奖金及社保停缴月份。
3. **尽快：** 核对失业保险资格，按属地渠道申请；并无全国统一“离职后第 7 天必须申请”的法定死线。
4. **当天查：** 看医保待遇是否正常，尤其核对领取失业金期间是否由失业保险基金缴纳职工医保。
5. **做笔账：** 近期可用资金 − 近期必须偿还债务，再除以家庭每月**必要净支出**。
6. **下周：** 找 5 位了解你工作能力的前同事/同行，告诉他们你想找的岗位和城市。
7. **两周后：** 看岗位匹配率、投递回复率、面试推进率；没收入时，不要盲目借钱创业。

**🔎 如果现在只做一件事：打开 [`index.html`](index.html)，按阶段勾完前三项。**

## 按时间读

| 阶段 | 优先任务 | 深度指南 |
|---|---|---|
| **失业前** | 校准市场身价、合法留存资料、谈 N / N+1 / 2N | [01 失业前](guides/01-before.md) |
| **失业后 7 天** | 离职材料、失业金、医保、公积金和家庭现金流 | [02 前7天](guides/02-first-week.md) |
| **失业 3 个月** | 精准投递、面试复盘、验证第一个付费客户 | [03 三个月](guides/03-three-months.md) |
| **失业 6 个月** | 经营净现金流、个体户 / 有限公司、自媒体与临时收入 | [04 六个月](guides/04-six-months.md) |
| **失业 1 年** | 家庭收支、家庭分工、城市与职业的重新选择 | [05 一年](guides/05-one-year.md) |

**城市政策单独维护：** [北京](guides/beijing.md) · [上海](guides/shanghai.md)。其他城市欢迎共建，不会用北京政策冒充全国政策。

## 粉丝怎么照着做（强烈建议先看）

**从这个入口开始：[0号指南：三分钟分流 →](guides/00-start-here.html)**。不需要从头读全部政策，也不需要公开工资流水。网站里选择自己的阶段、所在城市、离职原因和医保状态，给出对应办理顺序。这个分流**不判断你的法定资格**，资格由当地经办部门结合个案核定。

**每个任务都补齐了四块：**事情是什么、具体怎么做、什么叫完成、如果没办下来怎么办。做完要留下合法取得的回执、记录或可核验结果，不是看过就勾。

### 六份详细执行SOP

| 情景 | 你要拿到的交付物 | 直接打开 |
|---|---|---|
| HR突然谈裁员 | 工资、工龄、补偿金额与付款日核对表 | [离职当天与N/2N](playbooks/01-labor-exit.html) |
| 已失业，政策太杂 | 失业金办理记录、医保接续起始时间 | [失业金+医保](playbooks/02-benefits-insurance.html) |
| 下个月可能没钱 | 未来13周逐笔现金流、最低余额预警 | [现金流13周](playbooks/03-cashflow-rescue.html) |
| 三个月没面试 | 30个岗位记录、项目证据卡 | [求职漏斗](playbooks/04-job-search.html) |
| 考虑靠自己赚钱 | 10次客户访谈、一页服务说明、付费验证 | [第一笔付费](playbooks/05-first-customer.html) |
| 有孩子/想换城市 | 家庭周分工与双城成本比较 | [家庭重启](playbooks/06-family-reset.html) |

**常用空白模板：**[经办五问](templates/agency-call.html) · [HR沟通话术](templates/hr-conversation.html) · [13周现金流CSV](templates/13-week-cashflow.csv) · [岗位跟踪CSV](templates/job-pipeline.csv) · [客户访谈CSV](templates/customer-discovery.csv) · [服务说明](templates/first-offer.html)。

[GitHub发布与传播检查表](LAUNCH.md)；**对抗式审核结果：**[逐项反例、修复记录和仍未验证的边界](audit/ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW.md)。政策金额不是全体人群保底值，HR试算不是法院判定值，待批失业金不能当作已到账现金。

## 免费工具

| 工具 | 用途 | 是否联网 |
|---|---|---|
| ✅ **50 项任务清单** | 按时间 / 城市 / 关键词筛选，展开行动步骤，勾选完成 | 不需要 |
| 💰 **现金流计算器** | 粗算还有几个月生活缓冲，标明重复扣款风险 | 不需要 |
| 📅 **13周现金流逐周表** | 直接填确定流入/到期支出，预警第一周资金缺口，导出CSV | 不需要 |
| 🧮 **N/2N算术试算** | 校核工龄折算与工资数字；不代替法律适用判断 | 不需要 |
| 🗣️ **HR 沟通话术** | 先确认解除方式与支付安排 | 不需要 |
| 📤 **进度导出** | 把行动清单存为 TXT，继续线下执行 | 不需要 |
| 🔖 **15 条官方来源** | 方便查询政策原文及核对日期 | 点击外链需联网 |

### 如何本地使用？

下载仓库并**双击 `index.html`** 即可。无 Node、无依赖、无服务器，离线可用。任务勾选保存在浏览器 `localStorage`，没有用户账号或上传；现金流数字只在当前页面计算，不会发送到外部。

若要修改数据并重建页面，安装 Python 3.9+ 后运行：

```bash
python3 build.py
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
node tests/calc.test.js # 开发者可选；验证纯算法边界
```

项目架构：`data/guide.json` 是任务与政策结构化数据源；`assets/app.css`、`assets/app.js`、`assets/calc.js` 是 UI 与纯计算源文件；`build.py` 生成**自包含** `index.html` 和 **19份可直接手机阅读**的离线HTML版指南。提交时将生成的文件一并提交，读者无需安装工具。浏览器使用中所有个人数字留在本地。

## 两个最容易踩的坑

**“裁员就是 N+1 吗？”** 不一定。法律上的 N、代通知金及违法解除赔偿属于不同法律情形。具体依据 [《劳动合同法》](https://rsj.gz.gov.cn/zcfg/flfg/content/post_7993969.html)。

**“北京和上海，医保断缴都要等 6 个月吗？”** 不能一概而论。特别是上海 2025 年实施细则规定了灵活就业参保的 6 个月一般等待期，**也规定原本正常享受职工或居民医保、在中断 3 个月内转为灵活就业职工医保可免等待期**的情形。参见 [上海市职工基本医疗保险办法实施细则](https://www.shanghai.gov.cn/gwk/search/content/6173c838284f43c3b4d8c8d4513364ed)。

## 参与共建

政策会变，城市之间也不同。欢迎提交 Issue 或 PR，**但请给出官方原文、适用人群、生效时间、核验日期**。个人经历请去标识化；不收集身份证号码、手机号、劳动合同扫描件、工资流水等个人信息。

- [贡献说明](CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [城市政策模板](templates/city-policy.md)
- [离职沟通话术](templates/hr-conversation.md)
- [家庭现金流模板](templates/cashflow.md)

我们不接受没有来源的“包赔 N+1”“随便办个体户就能交社保”“兼职一定月入过万”等说法。

## 想找个人一起梳理下一步？

**作者咨询服务 · 按需了解。** 求职方向、简历与面试、职业转型，或 AI 应用与个人副业，都可以找 AI酋长 Andy 聊聊。

微信 **AIPMAndy** · [先了解 Andy](https://metaver.vip/)。添加时备注「求职咨询」或你想聊的问题，简单说说目前的情况。手册持续免费开放；咨询按需选择，服务范围与费用先沟通确认。

## 项目使用与授权

- **内容**（文字与数据整理）：[CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/deed.zh-hans)，转载请署名、给出仓库链接，标注修改。
- **代码**（HTML / CSS / JS / Python）：[MIT](LICENSE)。
- 政府政策链接和政策文本不因本项目许可而改变原有权利状态；本仓库主要提供链接和独立整理，不复制第三方网站图片。
- 受 [cdyforever/how-to-live-better](https://github.com/cdyforever/how-to-live-better) 的**单文件可搜索开源阅读页**思路启发，项目内容与代码独立创作，并非其 Fork。

**发起人：AI 酋长 Andy** · 欢迎补充有证据的城市经验。愿你的王国自由且富足。

a-funk/open-appleremote.text:
# open-appleremote

**Use the first-generation Apple Siri Remote on Linux**: the touch remote of the 2015 and 2017 Apple TVs (A1513,
A1962), not the older infrared Apple Remote. Touch surface, buttons and tvOS-style gestures are decoded in plain
Python 3 with no dependencies; an optional virtual keyboard makes an old remote work in Kodi, a browser, an emulator
or any other app, and the remote's microphone records what you say while you hold Siri (decoding it needs libopus).

Paired with Linux, the remote does nothing: BlueZ exposes it only as a raw `/dev/hidrawN` node with a vendor-defined
report map, and it stays silent until it is unlocked. This package unlocks it, decodes its reports, and turns them
into events, gestures or key presses. [docs/PROTOCOL.md](docs/PROTOCOL.md) documents everything it sends.

Status: 0.1.0, an early release, tested on an A1962 with Linux: finding, unlocking and reading the remote as a normal
user, and reconnecting after it sleeps. The virtual keyboard (`keys`) is not hardware-tested yet, and the voice
(`voice`, not released yet) hasn't run live: it is tested on synthetic captures, one of them built from another
project's recorded gen-1 frames. Reports are welcome (see [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md)).

## Quick start

You need Linux with BlueZ (its `hog` plugin is on by default) and Python 3.8 or newer. There is nothing to install:
clone the repository and run the commands below from its top directory.

**1. Pair the remote** (once). Hold **Menu + Volume Up** for about 5 seconds next to the computer, then pair it in
`bluetoothctl`. After `scan on`, the remote shows up named after its serial number; use its address:

```text
$ bluetoothctl
[bluetooth]# agent NoInputNoOutput
[bluetooth]# default-agent
[bluetooth]# scan on
[bluetooth]# pair AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF
[bluetooth]# trust AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF
[bluetooth]# connect AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF
[bluetooth]# scan off
```

**2. Let your user read it** (once), instead of running everything as root:

```sh
sudo cp udev/71-appleremote.rules /etc/udev/rules.d/
sudo udevadm control --reload && sudo udevadm trigger
```

Then press a button on the remote. The rules file explains the options for `/dev/uinput` and for headless machines.

**3. Watch it:**

```sh
python3 -m appleremote list # finds the remote's hidraw node
python3 -m appleremote monitor # decoded events, one JSON object per line
python3 -m appleremote gestures # tvOS-style moves, tilts and buttons
python3 -m appleremote lab # live web lab: open http://127.0.0.1:8791
sudo python3 -B -m appleremote voice --out voice/ # each Siri press as a WAV file: see Voice
```

The lab listens on 127.0.0.1 only. On a headless machine, forward it with `ssh -L 8791:127.0.0.1:8791 ` and
open the same address on your computer.

**4. Use it as a keyboard:**

```sh
python3 -m appleremote keys
```

This needs write access to `/dev/uinput` (root, or the optional line in the udev rules). The default key map:

| On the remote | Key |
|---|---|
| slide or flick up, down, left, right | arrow keys |
| click (press the touch surface) | Enter |
| Menu | Esc (back) |
| TV / Home | Home page (`KEY_HOMEPAGE`) |
| Play/Pause | Play/Pause |
| Volume + / − | Volume up / down |
| Siri | nothing |

Change it with a JSON file, `python3 -m appleremote keys --map keys.json`. Values are key names (`KEY_A` to `KEY_Z`,
digits, `KEY_F1` to `KEY_F12`, arrows, media keys: see `NAMES` in `appleremote/keys.py`), numbers from
`linux/input-event-codes.h`, or `null` to turn an input off:

```json
{"click": "KEY_SPACE", "siri": "KEY_C", "tv": null}
```

To start it with your session, see [systemd/appleremote-keys.service](systemd/appleremote-keys.service).

**No remote at hand?** `monitor`, `gestures`, `keys` and `lab` take `--replay FILE` to play a capture instead; all
but `keys` work on any OS. Try the lab with a real capture from the test data:

```sh
python3 -m appleremote lab --replay tests/sample.jsonl
```

Record your own with `python3 -m appleremote monitor --raw > capture.jsonl`: `--raw` also logs each report with its
time, which is what a replay plays.

## Events

`monitor` and `gestures` print one JSON object per line, ready for `jq` or any language:

```json
{"kind": "touch", "t": 0.0, "x": -849, "y": -828, "down": true, "fingers": [[-849, -828, 3]], "raw": "fc010032b8ff01af4ccc3e210a23"}
{"kind": "buttons", "mask": 128, "pressed": ["click"], "released": [], "raw": "fc0080"}
{"kind": "gesture", "type": "move", "dir": "right", "src": "flick"}
{"kind": "gesture", "type": "tilt", "x": -0.083, "y": 0.134}
```

- `touch`: `t` is seconds on the remote's own clock, `x` and `y` the first finger (+X right, +Y up, about 1650
 units across), `fingers` every finger as `[x, y, state]`.
- `buttons`: `mask` is the buttons held; names are `tv`, `volup`, `voldown`, `playpause`, `siri`, `menu`, `click`.
- `voicechunk`: an audio report while Siri is held. Through hidraw it holds only the start of an Opus frame: its
 level and sequence number, not enough to decode
 ([docs/PROTOCOL.md](docs/PROTOCOL.md#voice-opus-frames-cut-short-by-bluez-before-hidraw)). `voice` gets the whole
 frames (see Voice).
- `gesture`: `touch` (down or up), `move` (a focus step: `src` is `slide` or `flick`), `tilt` (a resting finger
 leaning the focused tile, -1 to 1).

From Python:

```python
from appleremote.decode import Decoder, Touch
from appleremote.device import reports
from appleremote.gestures import Gestures

decode = Decoder()
engine = Gestures(lambda kind, **f: print(kind, f))
for t, report in reports(): # survives sleep and reconnects
 for ev in decode(report): # Touch, Buttons or VoiceChunk
 if isinstance(ev, Touch):
 engine.frame(ev.t, ev.x, ev.y, ev.down)
 else:
 print(ev)
 engine.tick() # lets flicks coast
```

The gesture engine's feel (step size, pacing, flick speed, coasting) is set by the constants at the top of
`appleremote/gestures.py`.

## Voice

Hold Siri and speak: `voice` saves each press as a WAV file (16 kHz, mono) for whisper

ftop 
 A small, quiet system monitor for Apple Silicon Macs. One floating glass panel that works at any size. 
 
 中文说明 ·
 Download ·
 Install 
 

 

ftop replaces the terminal monitor you keep open in a spare tab with a native window
you can leave anywhere on the desktop. It is for the moments when the machine is
working hard — a local model running, an agent compiling, a long build — and you want
to see at a glance what the cores, memory, and network are doing, and which app is
responsible.

It shows the current state only: no history graphs, no disk panels.

## One panel, every size

Drag any edge. ftop picks the layout that fits and the window settles onto it, so
nothing is ever clipped and no space is left empty. A small window keeps the
essentials; a large one shows more, not bigger type.

 

## What it shows

Every figure is led by the same small round badge, and a badge with an arc is a gauge.
The color says what it belongs to; there is almost no text to read.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Cores** | One column per core, one group per kind of core the chip has, fastest first. The fill is usage; the tick is that core's current frequency. |
| **Memory** | Used and total, compressed, swap, and the system's own pressure level. |
| **Network** | Current download and upload speed. |
| **GPU** | A column of its own beside the cores, read the same way: the fill is usage, the tick is its current frequency. Memory in use and its watts sit below. Hover for its temperature. |
| **Power** | What the whole machine draws, in watts. |
| **Temperature** | One figure, labeled with the sensor level it really comes from. |
| **Processes** | The busiest apps with their own icons, helper processes folded into the app they belong to. An app's CPU is a share of the whole machine, the same unit as the total above it, so it never passes 100% (Activity Monitor counts one core as 100%). |

A reading the hardware does not give is shown as unavailable, never as zero.

 

## How it feels

- **Columns follow the readings.** Each core eases to its new value and arrives as the
 next reading comes in, so the panel moves continuously instead of jumping once a
 second.
- **A list that rests.** A process takes its place the moment it becomes busy and
 leaves it slowly; two apps trading the lead by a point do not swap. A row that
 passes its neighbor slides; one that goes further turns over where it stands, so
 rows never fly across the list.
- **Press a process.** The row gives under the pointer and a card comes up beside it:
 CPU, memory, and the helper processes inside the app. In a large window two badges
 switch the ranking between CPU and memory.
- **Nearly free when you are not looking.** Hidden or fully covered, ftop stops reading
 everything except the one reading in the menu bar.

With *Reduce Motion* on in macOS, all of this becomes plain fades.

## Settings

Right-click the panel or the menu bar number. One block holds everything: what to
show, how the panel behaves, the colors, and under **More** the few settings that have
a value.

 

The same settings are a plain text file, `~/.config/ftop/config.json5` (JSON with
comments). The two stay in step, and a saved change applies at once.

## Cost

Measured with `scripts/perf.sh` on a 14-core Apple Silicon Mac, updating once a second:

| State | CPU | Memory |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Small and medium panels | under 0.8% of one core | under 30 MB |
| The largest panel, 32 process rows | about 0.9% | about 52 MB |
| Hidden or fully covered | 0.0–0.1% | same range |

With system processes granted (below), the helper that lists them adds about 0.5%.

## Install

Requirements: an Apple Silicon Mac with macOS 15 or later.

**From a release.** Download `Ftop- -arm64.zip` from the
[releases page](https://github.com/Nongfsq/ftop/releases/latest), unpack it, and move
`Ftop.app` to `~/Applications`. Then link the command into a directory on your `PATH`:

```bash
mkdir -p ~/.local/bin && ln -sfn ~/Applications/Ftop.app/Contents/MacOS/ftop ~/.local/bin/ftop
```

The app is signed for local use only and is not notarized by Apple, so macOS blocks a
copy downloaded with a browser. Clear the download mark once:

```bash
xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine ~/Applications/Ftop.app
```

**From source.** Needs Xcode (built and tested with Xcode 27).

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Nongfsq/ftop.git
```

```bash
cd ftop && scripts/bundle.sh && scripts/install.sh
```

This puts `Ftop.app` in `~/Applications` and links `ftop` into `~/.local/bin`.

> **On 0.1.0?** That version cannot update itself. Install the latest release by hand
> once, as above; from 0.1.1 on ftop keeps itself up to date.

## Use

```bash
ftop # open the panel
ftop toggle # hide or show it
ftop quit # close it
ftop doctor # which readings are available on this Mac, and why not
```

- Drag the panel to move it; drag an edge to resize it.
- Move the pointer to the top edge for two buttons: pin (keep on top) and hide.
- The menu bar shows one reading, a glyph and its number: CPU by default, or memory,
 GPU, download, upload, or power (under **More** in the settings). Click it to show
 or hide the panel.
- Hover over a core, the memory bar, or the GPU for detail; click a process for its card.
- Right-click for the settings.

### Updates

ftop looks for a newer release once a day and installs it: it downloads the release
from this repository, checks it, replaces `Ftop.app`, and restarts the panel. Under
**More → Updates** you can switch this to *Tell me* (the update is then offered there)
or *Never check* (ftop never goes online). `ftop update` looks right now and
`ftop version` prints what is installed.

An update never changes the helper that `sudo ftop grant` installed. If a new version
needs a newer helper, `ftop doctor` says so and you grant again.

### System processes

Without extra rights macOS only lets ftop see your own processes. To include system
ones such as `WindowServer`, grant access once:

```bash
sudo ftop gr

## 怎么读

- **看到「别」「不能」开头的节名不用紧张。** 节名说的是这一节帮你防住的事（别进错公司、别把自己送进去），不是说底下每条都在让你别干什么。真正要做的动作写在条目标题里，一律动词开头，自己就写清了是「做什么」还是「别做什么」。
- **按性价比读。** 每节内的条目不是按时间排的，也不是按流程排的，是按「花出去多少、换回来多少」排的。最前面那几条通常不花钱、不费时间，先做这些。
- **按成本标签筛。** 每条标题下面有一行只有机器看得见的成本标签，把「钱」「时间」「毅力」三样标出来。你只想找不花钱的，就筛「钱=0」。
- **按口径分开看。** 每条说的是换回什么——钱、时间、健康、岗位还是人身自由。不同口径之间不做比较：一条省下两万块的条目，和一条避免刑事责任的条目，谁更值不值得做，没有统一答案。
- **只想看结论最硬的。** 在[在线检索页](https://goodseafly.github.io/how-to-make-work-pay/)里勾选证据等级 A，只留下引到法律、行政法规、部委规章和官方统计原文的 518 条。
- **只想看最值得做的。** 勾选性价比「极高」，得到 133 条既不花钱、不花时间、不需要毅力，收益又落在最大一档的条目。再叠加一个「换回什么」，就是该口径下的优先清单。
- **想按条件挑。** 打开[在线检索页](https://goodseafly.github.io/how-to-make-work-pay/)（想用本地那份也行，见下文「自己跑一份」），可以按关键词、章节、证据等级来筛，也可以按「花不花钱、花多少时间、要不要毅力」三样筛，几个条件能叠着用。页面上的内容直接取自 book/ 目录里的正文，正文一改，重跑构建脚本页面就跟着改。
- **想离线看、想发给别人。** 离线单文件版（高性价比职场指南-全本.html）整本书连同检索和筛选都在一个文件里，双击就开，不用服务器也不用联网，微信里也能直接传。
- **想打印或在手机上翻。** 用 PDF 版：A4 排版、五百多页，带目录页码和书签，每节另起一页。
- **想在 Kindle 或其他阅读器上读。** 用 EPUB 版（高性价比职场指南.epub），Kindle 用 Send to Kindle 发过去即可。
- **长文另见 docs/**：[被裁之后三十天](docs/被裁之后三十天.md)、[劳动仲裁怎么走](docs/劳动仲裁怎么走.md)、[入职前先查什么](docs/入职前先查什么.md)。长文把散在各节的条目按时间先后串成行动清单，每一步都注明出自第几节第几条，不引入正文以外的新数字。
- **条目之间会互相指路**（「见第 8 节第 17 条」这种）：检索页里这种指路带一条虚线，点一下就地显示被指那条的标题和「说人话」。在 GitHub 或纯文本里读，括号里写着指向什么，不翻过去也知道说的是哪条。
- **看法条看原文。** 每条「来源」栏给的是原文出处，法条带条款号。看「说人话」那一栏能知道大概意思，要拿去用就翻原文。

## 每条建议长这样

下面是书里真实的一条（第 26 节第 2 条），六栏都在：

```markdown

### 2. 让公司出书面解除通知，把解除依据写进去

 

- 成本：不花钱，要的是开口要一份文件。难在 HR 常常口头通知，你走了以后程序上什么都没有。
- 说人话：解除或者终止劳动合同时，公司要出具书面证明。公司只口头说一句让你走，你照常上班、照常打卡，别自己先撤。哪天解除、按哪一条解除，都要落到纸上。
- 收益：解除或者终止你的合同，公司要出具书面证明，还要在十五日内为你办完档案和社会保险关系转移。这份证明上要写明合同期限、解除或者终止的日期、工作岗位、在本单位的工作年限。无过失性辞退的，还要提前三十日书面通知，或者多给一个月工资。真打起来，举证责任在公司——它得证明自己说过什么、依据是什么。（依据：劳动合同法第四十、五十条；劳动合同法实施条例第二十四条；最高人民法院劳动争议解释（一）第四十四条）
- 证据等级：A
- 来源：全国人大常委会 (2012). 劳动合同法（第四十、五十条）. ；国务院 (2008). 劳动合同法实施条例（国务院令第 535 号，第二十四条）. ；最高人民法院 (2020). 关于审理劳动争议案件适用法律问题的解释（一）（法释〔2020〕26 号，第四十四条）. 
- 备注：证明里写「解除」还是写「你自己辞职」，会牵动经济补偿和失业金，见第 7 节第 14 条（并给你出解除证明）。公司不出证明的，找劳动行政部门责令改正，见第 12 节第 14 条（结清工资和社保转移）。通知、邮件、聊天记录怎么留，见第 12 节第 4 条（开始留证）。

```

`book/` 里每个节文件都是这个格式。改完正文跑一遍 `tools/check-body.py`，六栏缺哪栏、条号断没断、有没有裸条号，脚本会直接点出来。

## 自己跑一份

多数人用不着部署：离线单文件版双击就开。在线检索页 index.html 是纯静态的，`README.md` 和 `book/` 就是它的数据，没有后端、没有数据库、不用装依赖；注意 index.html 必须经 http 打开，直接双击本地文件会空白——浏览器不许网页读本地文件，那种场景用离线单文件版。

```bash
cd 高性价比职场指南
python -m http.server 8000
```

然后浏览器开 `http://localhost:8000/index.html`。把整个目录丢给任何静态服务器（Nginx、GitHub Pages、对象存储）效果一样。
